title: Nazism in Germany
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers only the Nazi rise to power and the Enabling Act, and it does not mention the persecution of Jews and others that the new point's brief includes, so adding that would be a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Nazism in Germany
card: The Nazi Party, led by Adolf Hitler, was a small party in the 1920s. The Great Depression brought mass unemployment and anger, and many Germans voted for it.
In January 1933, President Hindenburg made Hitler chancellor. Hitler used that office to end democracy.
After the Reichstag fire in February 1933, rights were suspended. The Enabling Act let Hitler make laws without the Reichstag. Other parties were banned and Germany became a one-party state.
The Nazis blamed Jews for Germany's problems and persecuted them, with laws such as the Nuremberg Laws of 1935. Others, including political opponents, were also persecuted.
draft.remember: Nazis used the Depression to win support, gained office in 1933, then ended democracy and persecuted Jews.

a.q: How did Hitler become leader of Germany in 1933?
opts: He was appointed chancellor, then ended democracy
He won a civil war against the elected government
He was elected president by a clear majority
He took power in a coup that failed the year before
a.why: Hindenburg appointed Hitler chancellor in January 1933, and he then used the position to destroy democracy. He did not win a civil war. His earlier 1923 coup attempt failed, but it was not how he gained power.
a.clue: Someone else gave him the office.

b.q: Which event best shows the Nazis ending democracy after taking office?
opts: The Enabling Act let Hitler make laws without the Reichstag
The Depression caused mass unemployment across Germany
Hindenburg appointed Hitler as chancellor in January
The Nuremberg Laws took citizenship rights from Jews
b.why: The Enabling Act removed the Reichstag's power over lawmaking, which ended democratic government. The Depression and the appointment came before this. The Nuremberg Laws were persecution of Jews, not the step that ended lawmaking.
b.clue: Look for the step that removed parliament's power.

a.best: He was appointed chancellor, then ended democracy

b.best: The Enabling Act let Hitler make laws without the Reichstag

problems.detail: The distractor 'He took power in a coup that failed the year before' implies a failed coup in 1932. The why correctly names the 1923 Beer Hall Putsch, so the option and the why disagree on the date. The option is meant to be wrong, but a student could leave thinking there was a coup attempt in 1932.

check.summary: Facts and answers check out. One small issue: a distractor in question a implies a failed coup in 1932, while the real putsch was in 1923, as the why says. Flagged as sensitive because the point covers the persecution of Jews.
